# Contributor Licence Agreement

Version 1, 2026-11-24.

Thank you for contributing to Animama. This agreement sets the terms for what
you contribute. You keep ownership of your work; the agreement gives the
project the rights it needs to publish that work and to keep licensing Animama
as a whole.

## Who and what this covers

- **You** are the person who submits a contribution. If you contribute on
  behalf of an employer or another organisation, "you" also means that
  organisation, and you confirm that you may agree for it.
- **The Maintainer** is Raymond Van, the owner of Animama, and anyone the
  project's ownership later passes to.
- **A contribution** is any work that you intentionally submit to Animama for
  inclusion: code, documentation, translations, artwork or other material, for
  example in a pull request to `raymond-van/animama`.

## 1. You keep your copyright

You keep all rights in your contributions. This agreement is a licence, not a
transfer of ownership, and you remain free to use your own work in any way.

## 2. Copyright licence

You grant the Maintainer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free,
irrevocable licence to reproduce, modify, publicly display, publicly perform
and distribute your contributions and works based on them, and to sublicense
those rights.

The Maintainer may license your contributions, as part of Animama, under any
terms. Today the public source is licensed AGPL-3.0-only, and everyone else
receives your contributions under the licence the Maintainer publishes them
with. The Maintainer may also offer Animama under other terms, including terms
that are not open source, for example in a hosted service or a commercial
edition.

## 3. Patent licence

You grant the Maintainer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free,
irrevocable patent licence, with the right to sublicense, to make, have made,
use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise transfer your contributions.
The licence covers the patent claims
that you can license and that your contribution infringes, alone or combined
with the version of Animama it was submitted to.

## 4. What you confirm

- Each contribution is your own original work, or you have the right to submit
  it under this agreement.
- If your employer or anyone else has rights in what you create, you have
  their permission to contribute it, or they have given up those rights for
  this contribution.
- If a contribution includes work that is not yours, you say so in the pull
  request and name its source and licence.
- You may use AI tools to help. You have reviewed what you submit, and these
  confirmations cover it in the same way.
- You will tell the Maintainer if you learn that any of this is no longer
  true.

## 5. No warranty and no obligation

Apart from the confirmations in section 4, you provide your contributions "as
is", without warranties or conditions of any kind. You do not have to maintain
or support them. The Maintainer does not have to use them.

## 6. How you agree

You agree by ticking the agreement box in the description of a pull request.
Your agreement covers that pull request and every contribution you submit
afterwards. If this agreement changes, the new version applies only to
contributions you make after you agree to it.

Questions: ray@animama.ai.
